out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Observed wet wiping cloths at the espresso maker in sanitizing solution at inadequate concentration OF <200PPM QUATERNARY AMMONIA.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. CFM REPLACED SANITIZING SOLUTION WITH SOLUTION FROM THE DISPENSER AT THE TRIPLE SINK WITH PROPER CONCENTRATION. EHS OBSERVED QUATERNARY AMMONIA AT 200-400PPM.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: UNDER COUNTER SHELF NEAR ESPRESSO MAKER NOTED TO HAVE EXCESSIVE BUILD UP OF DUST AND COFFEE BEANS.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. UNDER COUNTER SHELF MUST BE CLEANED PRIOR TO NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. OBSERVED NO CERTIFIED FOOD MANAGER PRESENT DURING INSPECTION. PIC IS NEW TO ROLE AND SCHEDULED TO TAKE CFM EXAM IN THE NEXT FEW WEEKS.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. PIC IS SCHEDULED TO TAKE EXAM IN UPCOMING WEEKS. FACILITY HAS AT LEAST 2 CFM ON STAFF. EHS WILL FOLLOW UP TO ENSURE A CFM IS PRESENT DURING ALL HOURS OF OPERATION AND THAT PIC HAS OBTAINED CFM CERTIFICATION. PEET'S COFFEE AND TEA (Inspection Date: 12/17/2024) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' OBSERVED EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY WITH NO EMPLOYEE SIGNATURES.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. PIC TO HAVE ALL. EMPLOYEES SIGN EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY OR PRODUCE CORPORATE EMPLOYEE HEALTH POLICY.

violations.title: Food Thermometer, Repair and Calibration
violations.observation: The food temperature measuring device was found out of calibration in the range of use. OBSERVED ALL THERMOMETERS IN FACILITY OUT OF CALIBRATION, WITH READINGS RANGING FROM 20F-45F IN A 32F ICE BATH (USING CALIBRATED THERMOMETER).
violations.corrective_action: Food thermometers shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. It is suggested that food thermometers be calibrated at least once a week in a cup completely filled with ice and cold water to a temperature of 32F or calibrated in a pot of boiling water at 212F. EHS SHOWED PIC HOW TO PERFORM THERMOMETER CALIBRATION USING ICE. EHS AND PIC WERE ABLE TO CALIBRATE ALL THERMOMETERS EXCEPT TWO. DISCONTINUE USE OF TWO UNCALIBRATED THERMOMETERS UNTIL ABLE TO CALIBRATE OR REPLACE.
